nodes.description: Specific intronic or structural alleles produce abnormal SNX14 transcripts, including pseudoexon inclusion, exon extension and multiexon loss. Nonsense-mediated decay is plausible for reduced RNA but was not directly established by these diagnostic studies.

nodes.description: In oleate-loaded SNX14-knockout U2OS cells, lipid droplets are fewer and more heterogeneous in size, with reduced total droplet area and modestly reduced ER contact extent. SNX14 remains anchored to the ER through its N terminus and contacts droplets through a C-terminal amphipathic helix; ACSL3 acts upstream of its recruitment. Total triacylglycerol, cholesterol and cholesterol ester levels were not significantly changed in this system. These results distinguish defective droplet maturation from universal failure of neutral-lipid synthesis. The route from this cellular phenotype to human Purkinje-cell death remains unresolved.

nodes.description: Two Hungarian Vizsla littermates developed rapidly progressive cerebellar ataxia at two to three months. Both had extensive Purkinje-cell loss, secondary granule-layer depletion and gliosis, with relative caudoventral sparing. MRI in one dog showed mild cerebellar changes. Cerebellar RNA from one case demonstrated a 275-base extension of exon 26; Western blot with an antibody targeting sequence upstream of the splice defect detected neither full-length nor shortened SNX14. The allele is strongly supported as causal, but parental genotypes were unavailable. The dogs were euthanized young, limiting assessment of later manifestations.

nodes.description: Neural conditional deletion bypasses the embryonic lethality of constitutive deletion of exons 9-12. This is distinct from the viable exon-14 frameshift model used for the 2024 lipid study.

Purkinje-specific deletion causes progressive Purkinje-cell loss, axonal swelling and motor deficits emerging at three to four months, supporting a cell-autonomous requirement for SNX14. Female animals showed greater severity. In contrast, Olig1-Cre deletion caused hypomyelination and mild Purkinje-cell loss without motor impairment through six months; this comparison limits attributing the full syndrome to oligodendrocytes alone.

nodes.description: In conditional Snx14-deficient mice, daily intraperitoneal valproate from P25 for 35 days improved motor coordination, Purkinje-cell survival and cerebellar respiration. Spastin abundance, microtubule organization and cultured-neuron mitochondrial motility improved. The tested mouse regimen was 250 mg/kg/day; this is not a human dosing recommendation. SAHA and panobinostat did not reproduce the rescue, limiting a simple generic HDAC-inhibition explanation. Human disease-modifying efficacy remains unestablished.

nodes.description: A subset of homozygotes survives to adulthood despite absent detectable SNX14; birth frequency is 9.9% rather than the Mendelian expectation of 25%. Adults have growth and facial abnormalities, mild gait changes, impaired complex motor tasks and social-memory deficits despite preserved social preference. Purkinje-cell loss appears earlier in anterior lobes than posterior lobes. Forebrain neuronal content is preserved, but cortical synaptic markers and phosphatidylethanolamines are reduced. Predegenerative cerebella accumulate acylcarnitines and show regional triglyceride reductions by MALDI imaging; bulk brain triglycerides were below detection in the separate LC-MS assay.
